newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL small-caps down, blue-chips up marginally.
newsitem.headline: KL small-caps down, blue-chips up marginally.

text.p: Malaysian stocks ended mixed on Friday, after Second Board stocks plunged almost 20 points before recovering some ground in the afternoon.
The blue-chip Composite Index was up 1.78 at 1130.59, while the Second Board index closed down 4.97 points at 595.58.

"The rebound on the Second Board could be due to punters buying stocks through Singapore where no companies have imposed restrictions on buying," speculated Teck Kwang, sales manager at brokers Jardine Fleming in Singapore.
Dealers said they were confident that the underlying fundamentals of the Malaysian economy were still on track for strong, sustainable growth.
"There has been no unnerving economic news recently," said Michael Auyeung, general manager of sales at HLG Securities.
Volumes were high again with 307 million shares traded, valued at 2,378 million ringgit. Decliners outnumbered gainers by 308 to 269, with 133 stocks remaining unchanged.
Construction giant United Engineers closed up 20 cents at 19.20, 10 cents below its year-high. Kwang pointed to foreign institutional buying of the stock for the rise.
